records.Concise description: OCEAN’s open-source protocol/gateway system that lets miners construct Bitcoin block templates locally while still submitting shares to a coordinating pool.
records.Deeper researched summary: DATUM moves transaction selection and block-template construction to a miner-controlled Bitcoin node/gateway while preserving pool-style share submission and reward accounting. OCEAN launched a public beta in 2024 and by 2026 shows active DATUM-mined blocks and deployment documentation. DATUM does not itself define OCEAN’s TIDES payout model; payout/accounting remains a separate pool-layer concern.
records.Launch / history: Public beta launched in 2024; active OCEAN deployment continued through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It provides a deployed alternative to pool-selected templates and makes the distinction between transaction selection, share coordination, and payout accounting concrete.
records.Verification basis: Current OCEAN docs/repositories and live deployment verify active DATUM use and miner-side template construction.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not generalize OCEAN’s TIDES payout system as a DATUM protocol requirement.
DATUM transaction selection remains miner policy subject to Bitcoin consensus validity.

records.Concise description: The original Bitcoin peer-to-peer mining pool design, launched in 2011 around a decentralized sharechain and direct miner payouts.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitcoin P2Pool distributed pool coordination across peers rather than relying on one central pool server. Miners contributed shares to a secondary sharechain and valid Bitcoin blocks paid participants according to the protocol’s recent-work rules. The original Bitcoin P2Pool network is treated as historical here; it must not be confused with the currently active Monero project also named P2Pool.
records.Launch / history: First released in 2011; its first mainnet pool block is documented in August 2011. The original Bitcoin network later became legacy/inactive relative to newer alternatives.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is the historical precursor for modern decentralized pool proposals such as Braidpool and an important demonstration that pool reward coordination can be peer-to-peer.
records.Verification basis: Historical Bitcoin documentation and current Bitcoin Optech context support P2Pool’s 2011 role and legacy status.
Research notes / uncertainties: Source confidence is MEDIUM because the original Bitcoin P2Pool source/site lineage is fragmented and modern search results frequently point to an unrelated Monero P2Pool.
Do not link the current `SChernykh/p2pool` Monero repository as if it were the historical Bitcoin implementation.

records.Entity / project type: decentralized Bitcoin mining pool protocol under development
records.Concise description: An actively developed proposal for a decentralized Bitcoin mining pool in which miners build their own templates and coordinate rewards without a conventional centralized pool operator.
records.Deeper researched summary: Braidpool is an open protocol/research project inspired partly by P2Pool but designed around newer consensus/accounting ideas. Current 2026 project and Bitcoin-development materials show active engineering and discussion, not broad production deployment. Its lifecycle is ACTIVE because development is active; deployment maturity is a separate field and must remain explicitly pre-production/experimental.
records.Launch / history: Developed publicly during the mid-2020s; active design and implementation work continued through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is a significant current attempt to decentralize both template construction and pool reward coordination rather than only moving transaction selection to miners.
Important technical or cultural characte: Not yet broadly deployed production infrastructure
records.Verification basis: Current project repositories and protocol discussion verify active development and intended architecture.
Research notes / uncertainties: ACTIVE means active development, not deployed network maturity.
Do not publish it as a production replacement for conventional pools without a dated deployment check.

records.Entity / project type: ASIC chip and Bitcoin mining machine manufacturer
records.Concise description: BITMAIN is a major ASIC designer/manufacturer whose Antminer product family helped define industrial Bitcoin mining hardware.
records.Deeper researched summary: Founded in 2013, BITMAIN designs SHA-256 mining ASICs and sells complete Antminer machines, control systems, power/cooling configurations, and related mining hardware. MSC models BITMAIN at the manufacturer/family level rather than creating separate profiles for S9, S19, S21, S23, or other individual Antminer models. AntPool is separate because BITMAIN states it was spun off in 2021.
records.Launch / history: Founded in 2013; early Antminer generations accelerated the ASIC-mining era, and current 2026 product lines continue the Antminer family.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin mining eco: It is one of the most influential hardware manufacturers in Bitcoin mining history and is essential for explaining ASIC chips versus complete miners, firmware, cooling, and pool relationships.
Important technical or cultural characte: Air, hydro and immersion-oriented product configurations across generations
Manufacturer is distinct from mining pool operator
records.Verification basis: Current BITMAIN site/catalog and company history verify active manufacturing, product lineage, and the AntPool/BTC.com spin-off history.
Research notes / uncertainties: Efficiency and hashrate figures vary by specific model and operating mode; never publish manufacturer-wide timeless efficiency numbers.
Do not describe BITMAIN as the current owner of AntPool solely from launch history.
